gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Synology rates the DS425+ for only 10 FSCT users (Microsoft's file-server capacity test), exactly the office's headcount, against 40 for the DS925+ and DS1525+/DS1525neo+. That gives a 10-person office 1.0× headroom on the DS425+ and 4.0× on the DS925+.
standout_why: computingforgeeks.com/best-nas-for-small-business (cited in chat 1) mentions a 40-connection SMB rating for the DS925+ but never relates it to headcount and has no DS425+ figure. It also has no power or running-cost numbers. Our own current page has per-user bandwidth (280 MB/s ÷ 10 ≈ 28 MB/s) and an all-in bill, but no FSCT user ratings, no cost per rated user and no power draw or yearly electricity cost. I couldn't load workcocoon.com/guide/best-nas-for-small-businesses (HTTP 404), so I couldn't compare against it. The QNAP and Synology spec pages ChatGPT cited contain the raw specs but don't divide them by 10 users.
decides: It confirms the DS925+ (or the DS1525neo+, which has the same 40 rating) as the Synology pick for 10 people. It also rules out the DS425+, which ChatGPT offered as the cheaper Synology in one chat (2026-11-13 19:58) and which our page lists. Synology reached its 10-user rating with the maximum 6 GB of RAM installed, and the unit ships with 2 GB, so a stock DS425+ has no headroom at all for this office. Power doesn't change the pick: across the four models I could source, yearly 24/7 electricity spans only about $36–56.

findings.label: Maximum Number of SMB Connections (FSCT-Based)
findings.note: Tested with maximum memory installed (6 GB per our page; ships with 2 GB). 10 FSCT users ÷ 10 staff = 1.0× headroom.

findings.label: Maximum Number of SMB Connections (FSCT-Based)
findings.note: Spec page: 'SMB performance was evaluated using Microsoft File Server Capacity Tool (FSCT) version 1.3'; max local user accounts 1,024. 40 ÷ 10 = 4.0×.

findings.label: What an FSCT rating measures
findings.value: Maximum number of simulated users a file server sustains on Microsoft's HomeFolders workload (Word opens, Explorer copies, deletes)
findings.source_title: “FSCT” - A CIFS/SMB/SMB2 File Server Tool for Capacity Planning and Performance Troubleshooting | Microsoft Learn
findings.note: Microsoft: results include 'the maximum number of users for a server configuration'; the workload was built from traces of real home-folder file servers. QNAP and UGREEN don't publish FSCT ratings, so these ratings only compare Synology models.
